Destroyers Announce 2025–26 Pre-Season Training Camp at APSU Stadium Led by Pranav Dwivedi

Rewa, MP — Destroyers Cricket Club (DES) have formally launched their pre-season preparation for the 2025 and 2026 Atal Bihari Vajpayee Memorial Tournament cycles, assembling an expanded 48-player training camp at Awadhesh Pratap Singh University (APSU) Stadium.

Skipper and all-round talisman Pranav Dwivedi, who has amassed 1,341 runs and claimed 63 wickets across 24 fixtures against arch-rivals Dread Eleven (DE), emphasized the team’s momentum following their decisive 4–1 series win in 2024.

"Our rivalry with Dread Eleven has set the benchmark for competitive cricket in the Vindhya region," Dwivedi stated. "With Aryan Deshmukh, Shivam Shukla, Anubhav Agarwal, and Venkatesh Iyer providing depth across all departments, our focus is squarely on sustaining championship standards."

The 2025 campaign will kick off with an intense four-match series in September 2025, leading into the Silver Jubilee Tournament edition in 2026 under the auspices of the Rewa Division Cricket Association (RDCA).

Dominant 2024 Campaign: How Destroyers Outplayed Dread Eleven 4–1 in 50-Over Series

The 2024 season of the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Memorial Tournament marked a watershed moment for Destroyers Cricket Club, as they recorded a dominant 4–1 series conquest over Dread Eleven at APSU Stadium.

After dropping the opener by a solitary wicket, Destroyers rallied in spectacular fashion: winning by 5 runs on 8 September (257/6 vs 252/7), edging a thriller by 2 runs on 12 September (276 vs 274), cruising by 18 runs on 16 September (288/6 vs 270), and sealing the finale on 20 September with an 8-run triumph (233/6 vs 225).

Captain Pranav Dwivedi stood tall throughout the campaign, delivering key middle-overs breakthroughs and anchoring crucial partnerships alongside Aryan Deshmukh and Shivam Shukla.

RDCA Unveils Upgraded Turf Pitches at APSU Stadium for 2025–2026 Cycle

Rewa — The Rewa Division Cricket Association (RDCA) has officially concluded extensive rejuvenation work across the central pitch square at APSU Stadium, ensuring international-standard bounce and seam movement for the 2025 and 2026 seasons.

Chief Curator Rajesh Patel confirmed that local red soil combined with clay blends from the Narmada basin was utilized to reinforce the wickets against weathering while ensuring equitable contest between bat and ball.

"Both Destroyers and Dread Eleven showcase fast-paced, modern cricket. These revamped surfaces will reward authentic strokeplay while granting genuine pace bowlers true carry through to the wicketkeeper," Patel stated.
